$comment: Ruby's canonical facts, answered once and reused in every vendor packet.
Fields marked "needsConfirmation": true were drafted rather than supplied and
must be confirmed before any packet built from them is sent. The packet
generator surfaces them as open items rather than silently asserting them.

entity.confirmationNote: State of formation and EIN not yet supplied; several vendor intake forms ask for both.

web.confirmationNote: Website URL inferred from the contact email domain and not verified. The privacy policy is a public Google Doc; host it on the company domain before submitting -- a docs.google.com link in a formal vendor submission reads as unfinished, and larger vendors' partner reviews notice.

application.name: Ruby
application.summary: Ruby prepares insurance claims for independent practices. It reads the clinical documentation a provider has already written for an encounter and assembles a complete, correctly coded claim for that payer, which the provider reviews and signs off on before submission.
application.userType: Provider-facing. Used by clinical and billing staff at the practice; not a patient-facing application.
application.accessModelNote: Population/system access authorized by the practice under 45 CFR 170.404(a)(4), typically via the client-credentials flow. Ruby is not a patient-directed app and does not use patient-context authorization.
application.confirmationNote: Redirect URI points at the internal management system host. Replace with Ruby's production callback before any packet is submitted -- a vendor registers this value and changing it later means re-registering.

requestedScopes.justification: Patient identity and demographics populate the subscriber and patient fields of the claim. A claim rejects on a demographic mismatch with the payer's member record.
Date of service, place of service, and encounter type are required claim fields and determine which CPT codes are billable.
Diagnoses supply the ICD-10 codes on the claim and establish medical necessity for the procedures billed. Missing or unsupported diagnosis coding is a leading denial reason.
Procedures performed supply the CPT/HCPCS codes and units billed.
Payer, plan, member ID, and coverage period determine where the claim is routed and whether it is within the filing window.
Rendering and billing provider NPI are required claim fields.
Billing entity, tax ID, and service facility location are required claim fields.
The clinical note is the evidence for the codes asserted. It supports the claim on submission and is what an appeal is built from if the claim is denied.

scopePosture.writeAccessNote: Ruby requests read-only access. It does not write to the EHR; the provider reviews and submits the claim from Ruby.
scopePosture.minimumNecessary: Scopes are requested per 45 CFR 164.502(b) minimum necessary. Ruby requests no resource it does not place on a claim or use to substantiate one, and requests no write scope.

security.statement: Ruby Health LLC is actively pursuing HIPAA compliance and SOC 2 certification. Neither is complete as of this submission.
security.auditLogging: Every PHI access is logged with actor, purpose, resource, and timestamp, retained for six years per 45 CFR 164.312(b).
security.confirmationNote: Stated as supplied: both HIPAA and SOC 2 are pending. Do not upgrade this language. Vendors ask, and an overstated compliance posture that turns out to be false is a materially worse problem than an honest 'in progress' -- athenahealth and other incumbents verify. The encryption and audit-logging claims above describe intended design and should be confirmed against what is actually deployed before submission.

regulatoryPosture.note: Ruby requests access as an API User under the ONC Health IT Certification Program's API Condition of Certification. Practice authorization is obtained separately from and in addition to vendor registration.
